paper.title: Parallelizing Exploration-Exploitation Tradeoffs with Gaussian Process Bandit Optimization

settings.name_in_paper: Parallel / delayed GP bandit optimization, f sampled from a known GP prior
unmapped: Feedback available at round t only up to round fb[t] with t - fb[t] <= B for a known constant B (batch size / delay bound)
Decision set D either finite, or compact convex subset of [0,l]^d with kernel whose sample-path derivatives satisfy a sub-Gaussian tail bound
Learner knows a bound C on the maximum conditional mutual information within a batch
settings.definition_quote: we assume there is some mapping fb : N → N0 such that fb[t] ≤ t − 1 ... In the following, we only assume that t − fb[t] ≤ B for some known constant B. ... One effective formalism is to model f as a sample from a Gaussian process (GP) prior.

source.quote: Theorem 1. Let δ ∈ (0, 1). Suppose one of the following assumptions holds: 1. D is finite, f is sampled from a known GP prior with known noise variance σn2 ... Then, the cumulative regret of GP-BUCB, using βt = exp(2C)αfb[t], is bounded by O∗(sqrt(T γT exp(2C)αT)) w.h.p. Precisely, Pr{RT ≤ C1 sqrt(T exp(2C)αT γT) + 2 ∀T ≥ 1} ≥ 1−δ where C1 = 8/log(1 + σn−2).

results.notes: Covers assumptions 1 and 2 of Theorem 1 (GP prior). Regret is realized regret sum f(x*)-f(x_t) bounded w.p. 1-delta. Bound depends on gamma_T, worst-case in the sense of not gap-dependent. Expression parsed from pdftotext; the sqrt is inferred.

source.quote: Theorem 2. Suppose one of the conditions of Theorem 1 is satisfied. Further suppose the kernel and T init are as listed in Table 1. Fix δ > 0. Let RT be the regret of GP-BUCB, which ignores feedback for the first T init rounds. Then there exists a constant C 0 independent of B such that for any T ≥ 0, it holds with probability at least 1 − δ that RT ≤ C 0 RTseq + 2||f||∞ T init , where C 0 takes the value shown in Table 1.
